author: ((Linnaeus), (1758))
summary: 지금까지 국내 기록이 10건이 안 되는 길잃은새다. 겨울에는 바닷가 가까운 얕은 만과 파도치는 연안에서 무리를 지어 지내며, 잠수해 홍합 같은 작은 조개와 고둥, 갑각류, 청어 알 등을 먹는다. 알래스카와 캐나다 북부의 호수와 습지에서 번식하고, 대부분 북아메리카의 태평양과 대서양 연안에서 겨울을 난다.

points.ko: 흰 판에 검은 점 있는 주황 부리(수컷)
points.en: swollen orange bill with a white side panel and black spot (male)
two whitish patches on the side of the face (female)
all-dark wings with no white patch

sexes.male: 온몸이 검고 이마와 뒷목에 흰 무늬가 있다. 크고 부푼 부리는 주황색에 흰색과 검은 점이 어우러지며, 눈은 희다.
sexes.female: 온몸이 짙은 회갈색이고 부리 기부와 귀깃 쪽에 흰 얼룩이 있다. 부리는 수컷과 모양이 같으나 회색이다.

young: 어린새는 암컷과 비슷하나 가슴과 배가 더 희끄무레하고 뒷목의 흰 얼룩이 없으며, 눈이 어둡다. 어린 수컷은 첫 겨울 동안 검은 깃과 뒷목의 흰 무늬가 차츰 생기지만 이마의 흰 무늬는 아직 없다.

art.subject: Surf Scoter (Melanitta perspicillata), adult male in winter, as seen from November to April: plumage entirely black, with a white patch on the forehead and a larger white patch on the nape; no white anywhere in the wing. Bill large and swollen, boldly patterned: a white panel on each side at the base enclosing a round black spot, the rest of the bill orange to orange-red; iris white; legs and feet orange-red.
art.pose: swimming in the surf near a rocky shore, side view
art.scene: Korean east coast in winter, breaking surf and dark rocks under a cold sky; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view swimming: entirely velvety black, white patch on the forehead and white patch on the nape, pale whitish iris, sloping forehead running into a large swollen bill, orange with a white panel at the base enclosing a round black spot, short pointed tail

adult female, side view swimming: dark sooty brown with a darker crown, two whitish patches on the side of the face, one at the bill base and one behind the eye, sometimes a whitish nape patch, dark eye, heavy dark grey bill with a squarish base

adult male, in flight seen squarely from above: head, body and tail in one line, wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, all-dark wings with no white patch, white forehead and nape patches, large orange bill
art.build: Medium-large, thickset sea duck, a little smaller than Velvet Scoter and bulkier than a Tufted Duck. Head large with a flat, sloping forehead running into a heavy, very deep-based bill, giving a triangular head-and-bill profile. Bill about as long as the head, swollen at the base in the male. Short legs set far back. In flight the wings are all dark with no white patch. Tail short and pointed, often held flat on the water.
avoid: Do not add a white wing patch; that belongs to Velvet and Stejneger's Scoters.
Do not forget the white forehead and nape patches, which no other scoter has.
Do not paint a slim plain dark bill on the male; it is massive and boldly patterned, with a black spot on a white panel.
Do not paint a rounded head with a steep forehead; the forehead slopes into the bill.
